analysis.title: Twilio Inc. (TWLO) 3Q26: Sequential Deceleration Raises Questions on AI Tailwind
key_insights: GS keeps a Buy on TWLO with a 12-month price target of $300 (prior $330) vs a $241.90 price, 24.0% upside. The target is based on 30x EV/EBIT (down from 35x on lower growth expectations) on SNTM (Q5-Q8) revenue estimates.
3Q26 revenue was $1,560mn, 3% above GSe and Street ($1,515mn each). 2026 revenue guidance was raised by 175bps and 2026 EBIT guidance by 5%.

GS attributes the negative stock reaction to two things: investors expected stable QoQ organic revenue growth, but it decelerated 100bps to 16%, and there are concerns about messaging growth durability into 2027 as compares get harder.

Organic revenue growth was 16%, down 100bps QoQ. Management attributed the slowdown to harder compares in messaging within the ISV business. Organic revenue guidance for the year was raised by 175bps.
Gross profit grew 18% YoY, flat QoQ and up from 9% in 3Q25, outpacing organic revenue growth by 200bps. Gross margin was 49%, 94bps above GSe.
DBNR was 114%, down 200bps QoQ. Excluding carrier fees it was 110%, down 100bps QoQ.
Initial 2027 guidance: organic growth above 10%, gross profit growth similar to organic revenue growth, and both EBIT and FCF of at least $1.35bn.

Voice revenue grew 20%+ YoY for the second straight quarter, driven by underlying minutes and software add-ons. Voice AI is only ~1% of Voice interactions, and adoption in regulated verticals (financial services, healthcare, insurance) is nascent.
Self-service revenue grew 30%+ YoY, including ~55% growth in self-service Voice. Management sees self-service as a leading indicator because AI-native customers often start there before scaling.
Software add-on revenue grew 25%+ YoY. Branded Calling and Conversational Intelligence are growing at triple-digit rates, and Twilio signed its first eight-figure Conversations deal.

Messaging revenue grew 24% YoY, including ~7 points from incremental carrier fees, or ~17% organic vs ~18% in 2Q. Management cited tougher comparisons at several ISV customers, not broader demand weakness. WhatsApp and RCS continued to grow quickly.
GS says messaging growth has been more opaque than Voice, particularly the drivers of different 4Q-1Q seasonality, and expects continued debate on the size of AI's impact on 2027 growth.

Personal agents are not yet a meaningful volume driver. GS sees them as longer-duration upside, but notes a risk that consumer agents could reduce email and messaging volumes tied to promotions and marketing.

GS raised 2026E revenue to $6,067mn (from $6,003mn) and cut 2027E to $6,744mn (from $6,767mn) and 2028E to $7,500mn (from $7,548mn). EPS estimates are now $6.17/$7.00/$8.15 for 2026E/27E/28E (old $5.96/$7.06/$8.39).

Buy thesis: Twilio benefits from shifts in the customer service market regardless of which application-layer player wins, and has potential for gross margin expansion as higher-margin products grow faster.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut from $330 as the EV/EBIT multiple falls to 30x from 35x on lower growth expectations. Buy reiterated, citing breadth of growth, installed-base expansion and early AI benefits.

3Q26 reported adjusted EPS $1.65 vs GSe $1.48 and Street $1.47 (+12% each), up 33% YoY.
3Q26 reported adjusted operating income $326mn vs GSe $290mn and Street $292mn, 21% margin, +39% YoY.
3Q26 reported gross profit $768mn vs GSe $732mn and Street $730mn, 49% margin, +18% YoY.
3Q26 reported free cash flow $370mn vs GSe $299mn and Street $312mn, 24% margin, +49% YoY.

tension_points.bull_case: Management attributes the 100bps organic deceleration to tougher comparisons at several ISV customers, not broad demand weakness. WhatsApp and RCS keep growing quickly, and Voice growth drivers are well understood.
tension_points.bear_case: Messaging growth drivers are opaque, including the different 4Q-1Q seasonality, and compares get harder into 2027. The stock fell because investors expected stable QoQ organic growth, and initial 2027 organic guidance is only above 10%.

tension_points.bull_case: Voice AI deployments are moving from proof-of-concept to production, enterprise customers are adopting multiple Conversations components, and AI-native customers start in self-service before scaling.
tension_points.bear_case: Voice AI is only ~1% of Voice interactions, regulated verticals are nascent, and consumer agents could reduce promotional email and messaging volumes.

theme_stances.key_argument: Management attributes the modest sequential deceleration mainly to tougher ISV comparisons rather than broader demand deterioration, and GS stays positive on growth durability.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to be positive on the durability of Twilio’s growth

theme_stances.key_argument: AI is progressing beyond AI-native customers, with Voice AI deployments moving into production, and GS sees Twilio in the early stages of benefiting.
theme_stances.evidence: Twilio remains in the early stages of benefiting from AI
